extracted.intended_audience: students, teachers, professional actors, and corporate trainers learning or teaching improv
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or producing short-form improv scenes using the Andy Goldberg / OFF THE WALL method, emphasizing listening, truthful play, character specificity, and emergent plot. Includes both high-level principles and an operational checklist for scene work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't Deny (accept offers / yes-and)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept what your scene partner offers (yes-and).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core principle: don't deny offers; accept what your partner gives you and build on it. Anti-pattern: blocking or contradicting an offer prevents the scene from progressing and kills opportunities for genuine play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, Don't Tell (embody choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the active choice; embody, don't narrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make choices physically and behaviorally rather than explaining them with exposition. Rather than telling the audience or partner what you intend, show it through action and physicality so the scene is vivid and immediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play the Moment (listen, don't pre-plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't plan ahead; LISTEN to what's happening now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize close listening and responsive playing instead of pre-planning jokes or outcomes. Playing the moment keeps scenes alive and allows authentic reactions to guide the scene's direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play the Scene Legitimately (truthful scene work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor comes out of the situation; be real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Play the scene legitimately and truthfully rather than aiming for gags. Let the situation's reality and stakes drive behavior; authentic play makes the audience recognize and laugh, whereas forced jokes feel artificial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't Try to Be Funny (authenticity over gags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funniness emerges from authentic play; don't reach for jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reaching for jokes kills the scene because it breaks truthful play. The audience laughs at recognition of real behavior and situations, not at obvious gags. Prioritize authenticity and the comic result will emerge naturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building Engaging Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Create characters with specific physicality, a clear point of view, and readable stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key concept: effective improv characters are specific in movement and physical choices, have a distinct point of view that informs decisions, and possess stakes the audience can understand. Use concrete physical details and consistent perspective to make characters engaging and to generate truthful interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot from Improv (emergent plotting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let actions reveal motivation; consequences accumulate and resolution emerges rather than being pre-planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't plan plot beats in advance. Allow character choices and in-the-moment actions to reveal motivation, creating a chain of consequences that naturally leads to a resolution. This accumulation of consequences gives improvised scenes believable arcs and satisfying payoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goldberg Method Rubric (operational checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: A five-question checklist to evaluate scene quality: listening, accepting offers, showing choices, playing truthfully, and specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational evaluation questions listed verbatim on the page: (1) Are players listening (not pre-planning)? (2) Are offers accepted, not denied? (3) Is the choice shown (embodied), not told? (4) Is the scene played for truth, not jokes? (5) Are characters and situation specific? Use these as quick yes/no checkpoints when assessing a scene or giving feedback.
